quirks: Danish military levy rolls (laegdsruller) begin in 1789 and enroll every male from early childhood under his father's name — each son's entry sits directly beneath the father's, making the rolls DIRECT parentage evidence for a male subject.
Danish naming is patronymic before ~1850: 'Mikkel Nielsen' means Mikkel son of Niels, so the father's given name is Niels — the patronymic alone does not identify which Niels.
Vital events are recorded in parish church books (kirkeboeger); baptism entries name both parents. Civil registration is much later.
The Stagstrup parish register is only ~3% name-indexed on FamilySearch — plan to browse the register images by year rather than rely on the index.

The dispute is over the first letter of the mother's given name in Cornelis's 1828 birth act. Three readings compete: "Jannetje" (the OCR of the birth act), "Fannetje" (the ten-year marriage index, a derivative abstract), and "Tannetje" (your own reading of the same image). Neither side outweighs the other.

Every record that could name the mother in full has been searched: the court's duplicate of the 1828 birth register does not survive; the 1850 marriage act is lost in both register copies along with its supplements; there is no death act for her or for Cornelis; her husband's death act also blots her given name; and there is no population-register entry, sibling birth act, or parents' marriage act. Nothing further can be searched to break the tie.

The mother is identified in the tree as Jannetje van Noord, with the proof summary reflecting this unresolvable ambiguity. The given name's first letter must stand as uncertain.

This new evidence connects to both existing hypotheses. Let me explain how it fits and what I need to move forward.

The death record names Robert Eastham's parents as **James and Elizabeth Eastham**. That's the same Robert Eastham who appears in the Burton household in the two census years — born about 1823, the person the second hypothesis says was likely Polley Burton's sibling.

Here's why this matters for the reevaluation:

The earlier Greenup County marriage record — the one for Mary Ann Eastham who married Ephriam Boggs in 1844 — listed her father as **Robert Eastham**, not James. So that Mary Ann's father was named Robert, while the Robert Eastham who lived with the Burtons had a father named James. For the second hypothesis — that Robert (b. ~1823) was Polley Burton's sibling — the death record adds a specific set of parents: James and Elizabeth Eastham. items.claim: Polly Burton (Mary A. Burton, Polley A.P. Burton) — Jahue B. Burton's wife shown in the 1850–1880 census records in Pulaski County, Kentucky — is a different person from Mary Ann Eastham, who married Ephriam Boggs in Greenup County, Kentucky on 30 January 1844. The FamilySearch profile LYYX-DS1 incorrectly merges these two distinct women.
items.notes: Primary hypothesis for q_001. The Boggs/Eastham marriage record (src_005, a_115) provides direct evidence of a separate Mary Ann Eastham who married Ephriam Boggs on 30 January 1844 in Greenup County — a woman who cannot simultaneously be Jahue Burton's wife Polly in Pulaski County. The 'Father of the Bride' Robert Eastham named in that marriage record (a_117) must have been born approximately 1795-1805 to have a daughter old enough to marry in 1844, making him too old to be the Robert Eastham Jr. (b. ~1822, Greenup County) who co-resided with the Burtons in 1850 and 1860. Four census records consistently name Jahue's wife as Mary A. or Polly Burton but never state an Eastham maiden name, providing negative evidence against the FamilySearch merger. The 1880 census image of the Burton household (log_021) documents Polley A.P. Burton's father as Virginia-born and her mother as Kentucky-born; these facts are recorded in the log entry but no formal assertions have yet been extracted from that image, so no assertion IDs for those parental birthplace facts are available here.

Burton's wife), both being children of a Virginia-born Eastham father and a Kentucky-born mother. This accounts for both Polley's possible Eastham maiden name and Robert Jr.'s persistent co-residence with the Burton family.
items.notes: Supporting hypothesis that would explain Robert Eastham Jr.'s appearance in two consecutive Burton census households while bearing a different surname. Key supporting pattern: Robert's sworn 1870 marriage bond (a_157, a_159) reports his father born in Virginia and his mother born in Kentucky. The bond is analytically superior — sworn self-report on an original document — versus a census entry from an unknown respondent with secondary knowledge. This conflict has not yet been formally registered in the conflicts[] section and remains open. NOTE on a_159 informant_bias_notes: those notes contain an error stating the conflict is with 'Polley A.P. Burton's 1880 census which shows the mother born in Virginia.' In fact the Burton 1880 census image (log_021) shows Polley's mother born in KENTUCKY. The real conflict is between Robert's own 1880 census (a_144, Virginia) and Robert's own 1870 bond (a_159, Kentucky). This error in the existing assertion should be corrected in a future assertions-only update.
